claims.statement: The W1 direct estimator (spike_w1/eta.py::estimate_vehicle) branches per event flag: flag in {1,2} takes the loop distribution P50 from dim_loop_remaining with no additive term (the car is already in a loop), flag=0 takes the mainline P50 from dim_remaining_time plus the pre-decision compensation p1·L1 + p2·L2 (dim_future_flag probabilities times dim_loop_duration); its resolve() falls back model→'ALL' and treats rows with n<30 as unavailable. Re-enters concentrate in the polishing stations 13/14/15IS065 upstream of the mainline, which is the rationale for the compensation.

The W2 v2 estimator (spike_w2/eta_v2.py::estimate_event) keeps the W1 ring branch verbatim (loop_rem P50, model→ALL, n>=30, no compensation) and upgrades the flag=0 branch with three mechanisms: line cohort mixing P50 = w08·P50_08 + w09·P50_09 (cohort rows n>=30, line-prob rows n>=100, missing falls back to the W1 rem table), rolling 8-week weekly p (weekly row n>=50 else full-window fut_all n>=30 else (0,0)), and comp exemption where (model,station) in comp_excl zeroes the p×L compensation.

The 'rolling 8-week' p and line probability are learned per replay week over the 8 ISO weeks strictly before that week ([Monday-8w, Monday-1d], no future leakage) by shifts.week_learning_range; 01_learn_v2 re-runs the ev_base + future-flag/lineprob SQL for each replay week over that range.

resolve_effective_flag (spike_w2/eta_v2.py) implements the docs/14 §5 v1.4 online dual-ring state machine as a pure function: R1 station in the 37-station UNIVERSAL_EXIT_STATIONS forces '0' (highest priority thaw); 139='2' passes only after a quadruple guard (137 bit must be '1'; spray-queue blacklist blocked before oven-out; pre-oven non-whitelist blocked; loop_exited guard); 139='1' maps to '1' only while not loop_exited (raw bits persist after exit, measured 96% of rework cars / 45% of blacktop cars), else '0'; everything else '0'. loop_exited defaults to False, reproducing pre-v1.4 semantics for the rollback path and replay tests.

The physical station sets are single-sourced in spike_w2/eta_v2.py and imported by W3: UNIVERSAL_EXIT_STATIONS (37 stations), BLACKTOP_ONLINE_WHITELIST (10 stations: report-entry cluster 6 + polishing line 4 incl. 14IS120), SPRAY_QUEUE_BLACKLIST (14IS260/13IS260), OVEN_OUT_STATIONS (16IS305/17IS305/18IS345 — the 2026-10-05 docs/14 erratum removed 20IS010 as a 2-line storage-line entry), and LOOP_EXIT_GATEWAYS (25IS010/25IS110/25IS210, the Doc14 v1.4 R3' loop-exit signal set).

estimate_event_unified (W4 unified engine) routes on the effective flag: branch A (eff in {1,2}) resolves loop_rem (station,eff) through the three-tier model fallback with loop_dur L as fallback, returns (None,False) if both miss, and sets eta = t + round(rem) with no additive term (constraint C8: loop_rem/loop_dur training targets are the full station-to-exit journey); branch B (eff='0') resolves the mainline base (cohort mix else rem), sets delay = 0 for the 37 post-gateway stations, otherwise resolves expected_delay (shift-tier table preferred when DSS_SHIFT_TIER_DELAY=1) with missing row falling back to 0, and returns eta = t + round(base + delay); comp_excl is not consumed by this function.

estimate_event_unified's effective_flag parameter is the offline purified-flag passthrough channel: when not None it skips the online state machine entirely. The replay side (02_replay_shift / 02_shadow_replay / unit tests) passes the purified flag from tmp_ev_base because offline purification is ground truth and the online machine is its stateless mirror; passing raw 137/139 bits there would kill all purified blacktop cars (fl='2') back to '0' and distort the G2 gate. The online predictor always passes None and runs the full state machine (agy blocker-3 fix).

resolve_hierarchical implements the three-tier model fallback model → LEFT(model,2) platform prefix → 'ALL' (empty/'ALL' model skips straight to ALL), accepting the first row with trailing n>=30; the mode parameter selects the consumed column: mode='shift' takes row[1] (mean/l_mean) and every other mode deliberately takes row[0] (P50/l) to prevent misuse. Learning-side tables generate exactly these three row tiers; the platform prefix list is measured from data and stored in learner meta (platform_prefixes), not hardcoded.

Column semantics (constraint C9, docs/14 §5): mode='shift' consumes the mean column because shift output totals are unbiased, mode='vehicle' consumes P50 because it is robust to per-car long tails. Consumers match: predictor.rem_of runs mode='shift' for shift output prediction and the dashboard single-car CLI runs mode='vehicle'.

The expected_delay row shape (delay_mean_s, delay_p50_s, n_fut, n_clean) has the column order REVERSED relative to the rem/loop_rem/loop_dur family (where P50 comes first); this is a known trap frozen in docs/15 §0.2: all consumers (unified engine, predictor, dashboard) must go through the dedicated resolvers resolve_expected_delay / resolve_expected_delay_shift with explicit indexing, and inline row parsing (generic row[0] take) is forbidden or mean/P50 would silently swap.

Both mode tiers of the net-delay resolvers consume row[1] = delay_p50_s, not the mean column (W4.4b revision, 2026-10-06): the G2 threshold-count measurement falsified the doc10 'shift-level additivity is unbiased' assumption because the delay distribution is fat right-tailed (mean ≫ p50 in 91% of rows) and the mean column pushed ETAs systematically late (mean arm 20.78% / -20.78% undercount vs p50 arm 10.60% / +0.71% ≈ unbiased); delay_mean_s stays in the table for diagnostics only, and the rem/loop_rem columns must not be p50-ized along with it (would worsen, cc 'bp' arm 11.17%).

expected_delay rows carry a dual-population dual-threshold gate: a row is usable only when n_fut >= 30 AND n_clean >= 30 (both populations), otherwise the resolver drops to the next tier (model → prefix → ALL → 0); this gate is independent of the generic trailing n>=30 gate used by the rem-family tables. The learner writes rows only where both populations meet the threshold (WHERE clause).

The adaptive takt factor α is applied exactly once, at the consumption point in predictor.predict's comparison (t + rem/alpha <= shift.end); no estimator embeds or consumes α, and the doc14 §5 pseudocode's tables.get('alpha') was explicitly rejected to avoid double scaling (B10): the rem returned by estimate_event_unified is the full base+delay caliber and α scales that whole rem once.

Engine gate semantics (docs/15 §0.5, .env.example): DSS_DUAL_RING defaults 1 (1 = W4 unified state machine + unified engine, production default; 0 = legacy estimate_event full path, the 30-second rollback); DSS_USE_NET_DELAY defaults 1 but is effective ONLY when DSS_DUAL_RING=0 (1 = old engine consumes expected_delay instead of p×L, doc10 retrofit; under DUAL_RING=1 the new engine always consumes net delay and the parameter is ignored, B11); DSS_SHIFT_TIER_DELAY defaults 0 (1 = unified engine prefers shift-tier delay rows; only the DUAL_RING=1 path is affected; 0 = shared row, zero drift). All three are strict 1/0: any other value raises ValueError at parse.

Zero-drift rollback discipline: DSS_DUAL_RING=0 with DSS_USE_NET_DELAY=0 is the bit-identical true rollback to pre-W4 (verified base_win 9.02% / 288-frame zero diff); DSS_DUAL_RING=0 with ND=1 alone is a half-migrated degraded state, not a safe rollback (W4.4f gate reconciliation). The legacy entrypoints (estimate_event, quality_mark, resolve_p) are deliberately kept untouched as the rollback path and existing test anchors.

Entry dispatch across the four consumers: predictor.rem_of (rolling pool) calls estimate_event_unified(mode='shift') with the full state-machine path (v.flag_137, raw 139 flag, passed_oven, loop_exited, entry_shift, effective_flag=None); the dashboard single-car CLI calls estimate_event_unified(mode='vehicle') deriving passed_oven/loop_exited/entry_shift as stateless own-trajectory single queries; 02_replay_shift._eta_pair and 02_shadow_replay's two static-side call sites both go through the shared estimate_for_replay dispatcher, so the rolling and static reference sides run the same engine and the G1 same-engine consistency gate holds (differences only from rolling pool/α state; under DUAL_RING=0 both sides run the old engine).

estimate_for_replay is the shared replay/static-reference dispatcher: DUAL_RING=1 → estimate_event_unified(mode='shift', effective_flag=purified flag, skipping the online state machine since replay does not maintain 137/passed_oven trajectory state); DUAL_RING=0 + ND=1 → estimate_event_net_delay (doc10 retrofit, flag=0 p×L replaced by expected_delay, comp_excl honored); DUAL_RING=0 + ND=0 → legacy estimate_event. It accepts an injectable dual_ring override for tests.

The online state machine's inputs ride on the pool, not the raw event stream: stream_pipeline.VehicleState carries passed_oven (rule O1: set True when the car hits any OVEN_OUT_STATIONS, monotonic, never reset), flag_137 (rule O2: latest-event value with '-' normalized to '0' on ingest/replay_car/adoptive paths — the 137 bit MUST be pooled, otherwise the online machine would kill all blacktop cars to '0' and paralyze the dual-ring engine, agy blocker-2), and loop_exited (v1.4: set at the three LOOP_EXIT_GATEWAYS, reset only on the new-cycle signal = re-entering an entry station). Invariant: these fields follow the car's own trajectory only (no cross-car contamination).

Under DUAL_RING=1 the replay contrast arm direct_nocomp was redefined as a net-delay-off baseline: the same event computed with both delay tables (expected_delay and expected_delay_shift) cleared to empty, measuring the net effect of the expected_delay table itself — because the unified engine has no p×L compensation and no exemption target, the old 'exempt vs not' contrast is degenerate (eta_d ≡ eta_d0, contrast always flat). Under DUAL_RING=0 the arm keeps the old comp_excl semantics.

The net-delay tables are learned by spike_w2/01_learn_v2.py (writes dss.dim_expected_delay W4.2c and dss.dim_expected_delay_shift W4.4h): population = the ⑥a full-window pre-loop population (flag=0 before the car's first flag 1 and first flag 2 event, same source as v2_future_flag — the clean-suffix population is structurally disjoint from fut=1 and must not be used); formulas delay_mean_s = max(0, P(fut)·mean(rem-base|fut=1) + (mean(rem_clean)-p50(rem_clean))) and delay_p50_s = max(0, P(fut)·p50(rem-base|fut=1)) with the baseline correction entering only the mean column and max(0,·) truncating only the final value; P(fut) reuses v2_future_flag week='ALL' p1 (rolling 8-week p deliberately not mixed, doc10 seasonal bimodality) and the baseline is same-source as the engine (dim_remaining_time p50 via the same three-tier join); three row tiers (body_type / LEFT(bt,2) / 'ALL'); the shift-tier variant adds the entry-event shift dimension (DAY [04:45,16:30) / MID [16:30,04:45)) without shift-conditioning P(fut).

dss.dim_expected_delay is a required table in the 14-entry startup completeness check (spike_w3/01_boot_online.py DSS_DIM_TABLES, added by W4.2c per B8); dss.dim_expected_delay_shift is optional — a missing table loads as an empty dict and the resolvers fall back to the shared row, which is exactly the gate-off behavior (zero drift).
